name: Eyjafjallajökull
description: Eyjafjallajökull is one of Iceland's most famous volcanoes. Its 2010 eruption caused widespread disruption to European aviation and demonstrated the powerful interaction between ice, water and magma.
geology: Located along Iceland's volcanic rift zone, Eyjafjallajökull is shaped by the interaction between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak, renowned for its towering near-symmetrical cone shape as well as inspiring centuries worth of Japanese art, literature and poetry.
geology: The stratovolcano is located on the Pacific ring of fire, at a triple junction between the Pacific, Phillipine and Eurasian plate.

name: Kilauea
description: Unlike other volcanoes, Kilauea erupts slowly and gently producing flowing 'pahoehoe' lava as opposed to highly explosive blasts.
geology: The shield volcano is fed by the Hawaiian hotspot - a lone mantle plume in the centre of the pacific plate.

name: Mount St. Helens
description: Mount St Helens is best known for its unexpected catastrophic 1980 eruption. An earthquake kickstarted a landslide, which triggered a sideways blast, devastating hundreds of square miles at hurricane speeds.
geology: The Volcano sits above the Cascadia Subduction Zone, where the partial melting of the Juan de Fuca plate results in magma-fuelled eruptions.

name: Etna
description: Mount Etna is Europe's most active volcano. Its frequent, spectacular eruptions constantly reshape Sicily's landscape and demonstrate the relentless power of persistent basaltic volcanism.
geology: Etna is a complex stratovolcano formed by the collision of the African and Eurasian plates, fueling its highly active and fluid magma system.

name: Krakatoa
description: The original Krakatoa volcano was destroyed in it's famous 1883 eruption, which is often described as 'the loudest sound in recorded history', heard up to 5,000 km away.
geology: Krakatoa lives on through Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa'), which demonstrates frequent, small eruptions.

name: Ojos del Salado
description: Sitting on the Chile - Argentina border, Ojos del Salado is the highest active volcano in the world.
geology: Ojos del Salado is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Nazca plate beneath the South American plate.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest peak in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.
geology: Mount Kilimanjaro is a complex stratovolcano formed by the East African Rift system, the same system responsible for most african volcanism today..
